seoTitle: Olbia cruise port guide: Isola Bianca, town and beaches
seoDescription: Ships dock at Isola Bianca; a free shuttle runs to the terminal, under 2 km from Corso Umberto. Bus €1 (2026). Porto Cervo is 30 km, 45–55 min in summer.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the Isola Bianca quays, the island's main ferry and cruise port, and you cannot walk across the port area: a free port shuttle takes you to the Stazione Marittima at the port exit. From there the centre around Corso Umberto is under 2 km, by foot, ASPO bus 9 (€1 if bought before boarding, 2026) or taxi. Be back at the terminal 60 minutes before all-aboard, and 90 if you go to the Costa Smeralda.
intro: Olbia is Sardinia's main gateway in the north-east, and its port is built for ferries as much as cruise ships. Passengers cannot walk through the Isola Bianca port area, so the first part of the day is the port shuttle and the run into town. The centre is small and low-key: Corso Umberto, the Romanesque basilica of San Simplicio and an archaeological museum of Roman shipwrecks on an islet by the old port. Most passengers come for what lies outside: sandy beaches such as Pittulongu close by, and the Costa Smeralda and Porto Cervo about 30 km to the north, where summer traffic is the main risk to your return.

terminals.name: Isola Bianca quays and Stazione Marittima (maritime station)
terminals.notes: Isola Bianca has ten quays serving ferries, ro-ro ships and cruise ships. Passengers may not walk through the port area, so a free shuttle bus runs between the ship and the maritime station at the port exit. The station has a bar, restaurant, tobacconist, ticket offices and a port information desk, and a 24-hour first-aid service in summer. Security screening is on the way back to the ship. The centre is under 2 km away.

walkability.detail: The quay itself is not walkable: take the free port shuttle to the maritime station. From the station the centre is under 2 km by road. Fit walkers can do it, but port traffic and summer heat make the bus or a taxi the easier choice. Once in the centre, Corso Umberto, San Simplicio and the old port are all walkable.

transportSections.detail: Runs inside the port area between the ship's berth and the Stazione Marittima at the port exit. Walking across the port is not allowed.

Links the maritime station with the railway station via Corso Umberto I. Line 9 also stops in front of the town hall, near the Archaeological Museum. Buy tickets before boarding to pay the lower fare.

Taxi ranks are at the port, on Corso Umberto and at the airport. For the Costa Smeralda, agree the fare and a return time in advance; regular taxis to Porto Cervo from the airport area cost about €90–120 one way (2026).
Summer-only bus from the centre to Pittulongu beach, roughly every 30 minutes.

Regional buses leave from the square in front of the maritime station. Services to resort towns are less frequent than city buses and timings often suit cruise passengers poorly; check the ARST timetable before relying on one.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the Stazione Marittima 60 minutes before all-aboard (16:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard); 90 minutes if you have been to the Costa Smeralda.
returnTiming.detail: You still need to clear security and ride the port shuttle back to the ship, and ferry departures can make the port roads busy. Porto Cervo is about 30 km from Olbia; in July and August the drive can take 45–55 minutes because of afternoon traffic, so leave the coast early.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from the rank on Corso Umberto straight to the port. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

excursionAdvice: Skip the ship tour for Olbia itself and for a beach close to town: the port shuttle, bus 9 and the summer beach bus are cheap and simple. The ship's tour is worth it for the Costa Smeralda, Porto Cervo, La Maddalena or Tavolara. Public buses to the resorts are infrequent, taxis are expensive, and summer traffic on the coast road can turn a 30 km drive into close to an hour, so a tour with a guaranteed return removes the main risk of the day.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30, on a summer day.

steps.what: Free port shuttle to the Stazione Marittima, then bus 9 or a taxi into the centre.
Archaeological Museum on the islet by the old port (opens 08:00, closed Sundays and Mondays): Roman shipwrecks from the ancient harbour.
Walk up Corso Umberto I and the lanes around it; see the tiled dome of San Paolo.
Basilica of San Simplicio (Monday to Saturday 10:00–17:00), the city's Romanesque granite church.
Lunch in the centre: fregola with clams, or Olbia mussels.
Line 40 Spiagge Express to Pittulongu for a swim (summer), or stay in town for cafés and shops.
Bus back from Pittulongu to the centre, then bus 9 or a taxi to the port.
At the Stazione Marittima, clear security and take the shuttle to the ship, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Archaeological Museum of Olbia
sights.why: Two of the eleven Roman merchant ships burned in the ancient port around 450 AD, with full-size reconstructions and a 180-degree film of the Vandal attack.
sights.tip: On the islet of Peddone by the old port. Listed hours are Tuesday to Saturday, 08:00–13:00 and 16:00–19:00, so plan it for the morning.

sights.name: Basilica of San Simplicio
sights.why: Romanesque granite church whose forms date from the 12th century, the oldest Christian monument in the area and the city's patron church.
sights.tip: Open Monday to Saturday, 10:00–17:00. Phone +39 0789 396241 to check before going.

sights.name: Corso Umberto I and the historic centre
sights.why: The main street of shops, cafés and restaurants, with small squares off it.
sights.tip: Bus 9 from the port runs along it; start at the old-port end and walk inland.

sights.name: Church of San Paolo Apostolo
sights.why: Baroque church with a tiled ceramic dome, a short walk from San Simplicio.
sights.tip: Combine it with San Simplicio and Corso Umberto.

sights.name: Punic walls and Roman remains
sights.why: Traces of the Punic town walls and towers on Via Torino and Roman forum remains near the town hall.
sights.cost: Free to view from the street
sights.tip: Easy to fit between the museum and Corso Umberto.

sights.name: Porto Cervo and the Costa Smeralda
sights.why: The resort coast north of Olbia, with the yacht marina and promenade of Porto Cervo.
sights.cost: Taxi about €90–120 each way (2026), or a ship's tour
sights.tip: About 30 km away; allow 45–55 minutes each way in July and August.

sights.name: Tavolara
sights.why: A huge granite island in the protected Tavolara marine area, good for snorkelling.
sights.tip: Boats leave from Porto San Paolo, south of Olbia, so it is best done as a tour on a cruise day.

beaches.name: Pittulongu (La Playa)
beaches.howToGetThere: ASPO line 40 Spiagge Express from the centre (summer)
beaches.note: The nearest sandy beach to town. Bring your own towel; sunbed hire is expensive.

beaches.name: Bados and Pellicano
beaches.note: Beaches on the coast north-east of Olbia beyond Pittulongu.

beaches.name: Le Saline, Lido del Sole and Li Cuncheddi
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi south on the SS125 towards San Teodoro
beaches.note: Sandy beaches south of the city; check summer traffic before you go.

beaches.name: Porto Istana
beaches.note: Four small bays within a protected area facing Tavolara.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to walk off the ship across the port.
commonMistakes.fix: Walking in the port area is not allowed. Take the free shuttle to the Stazione Marittima first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the Costa Smeralda is a short hop.
commonMistakes.fix: Porto Cervo is about 30 km away and the drive can take 45–55 minutes in summer. Book a tour or leave the coast early.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on regional buses to resorts for the return.
commonMistakes.fix: ARST services are infrequent and often badly timed for cruise calls. Use a taxi with an agreed pick-up or a ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying the bus 9 ticket on board.
commonMistakes.fix: It costs €1.50 on board against €1 bought in advance (2026). Buy at the station or a tobacconist.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Archaeological Museum for the afternoon or a Monday.
commonMistakes.fix: It closes at lunchtime and on Sundays and Mondays. Go in the morning, Tuesday to Saturday.

safety: Olbia is a working port city and safe for visitors. Take care on the port roads, which carry heavy ferry and lorry traffic, and do not walk inside the port area. In summer the heat is the main problem on the walk into town and at the beaches, so carry water and sun protection. Check beach flags and sea conditions before swimming. Use licensed taxis from the ranks rather than unlicensed transport offers.
accessibility: Olbia is a docked port and the free port shuttle connects the ship with the terminal; ask the ship about accessible transfers on the day. The centre around Corso Umberto is flat. The Archaeological Museum is on an islet reached on foot from the old port; check access by phone on +39 340 3560742 during opening hours.
rainyDay: Spend the morning in the Archaeological Museum, which is large enough for a long visit, then San Simplicio and San Paolo, with lunch and cafés on and around Corso Umberto. Skip the beaches and the coastal drive.
crowdTips: Olbia is a very busy ferry port as well as a cruise port. In peak season (June to September) go to the beaches early in the morning. The Costa Smeralda roads are slowest in the afternoon in high summer, so do the coast in the morning and town in the afternoon, not the other way round.

faqs.a: No. Ships dock at the Isola Bianca quays, and a free port shuttle takes you to the maritime station.

faqs.q: Is Olbia walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Partly. You must take the free shuttle across the port first. From the maritime station the centre is under 2 km, but most people take bus 9 or a taxi.

faqs.q: How do I get from Olbia cruise port to the town centre?
faqs.a: Free port shuttle to the Stazione Marittima, then ASPO bus 9 along Corso Umberto (€1 in advance, €1.50 on board, 2026), a taxi, or a walk of under 2 km.

faqs.q: Can I visit Porto Cervo from Olbia cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes, but allow time. It is about 30 km away and the drive takes 45–55 minutes in July and August. A taxi costs about €90–120 each way (2026), so a ship's tour is often simpler.
Pittulongu is the closest, about 15 minutes by the summer line 40 bus (€5 return, 2026). Le Saline, Lido del Sole and Porto Istana are about 10 km south by taxi.

faqs.q: What can I do in Olbia in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Archaeological Museum, San Simplicio, Corso Umberto and a swim at Pittulongu, or a tour to the Costa Smeralda or Tavolara.
Yes. Take care with port traffic and summer heat, and use licensed taxis.
